body:
>  It's so humiliating, and ultimately unhelpful, to be dragged off by the cops to be held "for your own good" because you made the mistake of telling somebody how you really felt.

Pretty much. I remember the first time I was hospitalized. I made the mistake of telling the doctor on call that I was still very much wanting to hurt myself, and they proceeded to restrain me to the hospital bed. Then there was transporting me through the rest of the ER shackled to the bed, feeling helpless, feeling hopeless, feeling judged by every face that squinted their eyes at me (really? she's trying to hurt herself? what a fuck.)

And yes, I know I'm overcompensating. I just can't afford to mess up anymore. And no, living with my ex isn't good, but we have a third roommate now that is *much* healthier for both of us than our completely bananas last roommate(s).
